newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AKZO NOBEL TO BUILD AUSTRALIAN SALT PLANT.
newsitem.headline: AKZO NOBEL TO BUILD AUSTRALIAN SALT PLANT.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Wednesday it would invest 50 million US dollars in building a solar salt facility in western Australia.
"The project will be realised with Australian and Asian partners," the Dutch company said without identifiying the partners.
The Onslow-based plant will serve the growing chemical industry in the area and will come on stream in 1999.
Construction of the plant, which will produce salt from sea water, will start after the authorities have granted the necessary permits, which is expected in the second quarter of 1997.

Akzo Nobel said the facility will initially have annual production capacity of 2.5 millions tonnes but added it will have substantial expansion possibilities. The unit will employ more than 50 people in Onslow and its Perth office.
